72148.guideline_authority: CMS LCD L34220 / American College of Radiology (ACR) Appropriateness Criteria
medical_necessity_criteria: Lower extremity radicular pain corresponding to specific dermatome with neurological signs (reflex change, sensory loss, motor weakness).
Failure of conservative therapy (minimum 6 weeks) OR immediate imaging indicated when progressive motor deficit or red flag symptoms are present.
Evaluation for surgical candidate or epidural steroid injection planning.
72148.appeal_argument_template: The adverse determination citing lack of conservative therapy is clinically unfounded. As documented in clinical records, patient completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy without resolution. Furthermore, under ACR Appropriateness Criteria, the presence of progressive motor weakness (extensor hallucis longus 4/5) qualifies as a clinical exception waiving any prior conservative therapy requirement due to risk of permanent neurological deficit.
statutory_citations: 29 C.F.R. § 2560.503-1(h)(3)(iii) (Consultation with independent health care professional with appropriate training)

J0135.guideline_authority: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) Clinical Guidelines for Crohn's Disease
medical_necessity_criteria: Moderate to severely active Crohn's disease with documented mucosal inflammation.
Step therapy override is clinically warranted when preferred agents are medically contraindicated, caused prior adverse reactions, or are clinically ineffective.
J0135.appeal_argument_template: The denial based on fail-first step therapy violates standard clinical care and plan fiduciary duties. Under ACG Clinical Guidelines and state/federal step therapy exception statutes, step therapy must be overridden when the preferred alternatives are clinically contraindicated. Patient previously suffered documented drug-induced hepatotoxicity from azathioprine and pancytopenia from methotrexate. Forcing re-trial of toxic agents violates medical safety.
statutory_citations: 29 C.F.R. § 2560.503-1(h)(2)(iv) (Entitlement to all internal criteria and rules relied upon)
